= ACE blocked-mode CRC failure: distance-history fix — 2026-11-07 =

== Result ==

The `-2` patterned-input failure is a decompression/data-round-trip defect, not an
incorrect CRC-32 calculation and not CyberChef's separate ACE header CRC-16
check. A separate source patch fixes the defect in the external
[`seb3773/ace-c`](https://github.com/seb3773/ace-c) encoder. It does **not** alter
this repository's ACE header parser.

The earlier 2026-11-04 experiment note did not preserve the original temporary
fixture generator, so that exact byte sequence could not be replayed. A
repeatable representative varying-offset fixture was reconstructed and produces
the same reported failure class:

```python
n = 131072
input[i] = ((i % 7) + (i // 7)) & 0xff
```

At base commit `6cc986fbecf65137bc4657039fba1eb227e2e446`, `ace a ... -2 ...`
followed by `ace t` reports `crc mismatch` for this fixture. The same happens
with only the two-queue Huffman patch applied. The same input passes `-z`
integrity testing and extraction. The new regression script also checks period-13
and period-64 variants.

== Diagnosis ==

The CRC routine's raw ACE CRC-32 variant is consistent between archive writing
and verification. Extraction produces wrong bytes after a blocked-mode boundary.
The compressor called `tokenize()` separately for each blocked LZ77/DELTA run;
`tokenize()` reset its four-entry repeat-distance history every time. The decoder
keeps that history in `ace_lz77_t.dh` across typecode/mode switches. Thus, a
repeated-distance symbol in a later run could refer to a different distance at
decode time than the encoder used. The Huffman tree change was not causal: it
changes code lengths/tie ordering, while leaving this token-history mismatch
unchanged.

The fix owns and zero-initializes the repeat-distance history once per compressed
member, then passes that shared state through each tokenization call. It aligns
the encoder with the decoder's existing state lifetime; it does not weaken or
bypass any CRC check.

== Patch and verification ==

- [`patches/ace-c-lz77-distance-history.patch`](../patches/ace-c-lz77-distance-history.patch)
  — separate patch against `ace-c` base commit `6cc986f`; it changes only
  `src/compress.c` when applied.
- [`scripts/test-ace-c-distance-history-fix.sh`](../scripts/test-ace-c-distance-history-fix.sh)
  — builds a temporary checkout, confirms the `-z` control, reproduces the
  baseline and Huffman-only `-2` CRC failures, applies the distance-history fix,
  and verifies `ace t`, extraction, and byte-for-byte `cmp` for three fixtures.
- Run with:

  ```sh
  ACE_C_DIR=/path/to/ace-c ./scripts/test-ace-c-distance-history-fix.sh
  ```

Verified in this workspace: baseline and Huffman-only builds both reproduced the
CRC mismatch; the combined two-queue Huffman plus distance-history build passed
`test_core` and all three `-2` integrity/extraction comparisons. The existing
[`scripts/test-ace-c-huffman-patch.sh`](../scripts/test-ace-c-huffman-patch.sh)
also passed its 14,150 Huffman vectors and five archive round trips.

== Scope and remaining caveats ==

This is a source-level fix for the independent `ace-c` implementation, not a
patch to CyberChef's header-CRC code or a change to this repository's ACE parser.
The reconstructed fixture is a confirmed representative reproducer, but the
exact earlier temporary fixture was not saved, so this does not claim a
bit-for-bit replay of that original run. Independent WinACE-compatible reader
testing, third-party ACE corpus testing, cross-version testing, and original
WinACE executable disassembly remain open validation gates. The Huffman patch
also retains its separate tie-order/interoperability caveat.
